relevance.rationale: A long review of the Magnus expansion: representing the solution of a linear system with varying coefficients as a single exponential of a series of nested commutators, with existence and convergence theorems, an improved radius of convergence, the relation to BCH, the Fer and Wei-Norman product alternatives, and the connection to the Chen-Fliess series. The folio's mass identity is the norm of a nonabelian multiplicative integral (Yekutieli), and prop:mi-sw-abelianisation's authorNotes record that no Lean instance is expected because the construction needs nonabelian gauge theory and Yekutieli multiplicative integration -- so a computable, convergence-controlled representation of a path-ordered product is squarely on the folio's critical path. Supporting rather than core, for a specific reason: the corpus's MI is SURFACE-ordered (an integral over an exceptional divisor, requiring nonabelian Stokes), whereas Magnus is the theory of the path-ordered (one-dimensional) case, which this review does not extend to surface ordering. So it supplies technique for a sub-problem, not for the stated object. Corpus-grep over content/, docs/, computations/: no Magnus, Fer, BCH or Chen-Fliess material exists anywhere, so this is an absence rather than a duplicate.

keyResults.statement: Existence of the Magnus exponent and convergence of the Magnus series, with an improved radius of convergence in terms of the integrated operator norm.
keyResults.useForFolio: A proved convergence criterion for the exponential representation of a path-ordered transport -- the kind of statement that could make a Lean-tractable sub-case of the MI machinery, in contrast to the current position that no instance is expected. What would need checking: whether the corpus's connection-curvature pair restricted to a path in the exceptional divisor satisfies the norm bound.

keyResults.locator: Sect. 3.5 (Magnus expansion and the Chen-Fliess series)
keyResults.statement: The relation between the Magnus exponent and the Chen-Fliess series of iterated integrals.
keyResults.useForFolio: Chen iterated integrals are the algebraic backbone of the shuffle Hopf algebra the corpus builds its level-2 primitive on; this is an explicit bridge between that combinatorial side and the analytic transport side, which the folio currently keeps separate.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry and no Magnus/BCH/Chen-Fliess material anywhere in the corpus, despite the mass identity being defined through a nonabelian multiplicative integral.

Record the path-ordered Magnus representation and its convergence criterion next to prop:mi-sw-abelianisation's no-instance note, stating plainly that Magnus covers the one-dimensional case only and that the surface-ordered case the corpus needs is not addressed here. Deliberately not aid-proof: the dimension mismatch is exactly the unchecked hypothesis.
